A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAIL-VL and SAIL-Caption research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding figures, tables and analyses can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, data-quality comparisons, scaling analyses and ablations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds human evaluations of caption quality and SFT-stage data characteristics.

M1.justification: The five-stage training procedure, parameter-freezing strategy and data-curation algorithms remain the same. Naming the captioner backbone and explaining curation steps more explicitly supplies documentation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: The English/Chinese caption and OCR coverage, three SFT stages and 18-benchmark evaluation suite are retained. Human assessments concern existing corpora; newly named source examples do not establish additional task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same VLM baselines, caption datasets, SFT datasets and all-in-one training baseline. InternVL2, InternVL2.5 and Aquila already appear in v2's appendix; v3's human caption evaluation uses the existing caption-comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds human caption reviews on 100 samples per dataset alongside the retained 500-sample GPT evaluations, using absolute ratings, Good-Same-Bad judgments and an annotation audit. It also introduces SFT-quality rating rubrics. The OCR ablation condition labelled LQ in v2 Table 4 becomes HQ+LQ in v3 Table 5, a reported setting revision without evidence of rerunning.

E4.justification: Data-quality validation expands substantially: Appendix D adds human caption ratings and pairwise comparisons, while Table 2 and Appendix F assess difficulty, complexity and relevance across SFT stages. These provide additional evidence for two central data-quality arguments. Existing OCR-quality and 2M-sample SFT ablations remain, and Figure 5's curriculum-versus-AIO analysis is revised.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The Pearson correlation and R-squared reporting is unchanged. v3's 95%+ annotation-check accuracy is an evaluation result, not a confidence level or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: v3 adds human caption and SFT-quality results and materially revises the curriculum comparison. Figure 5 raises final AIO performance from 67.2 to approximately 68.38, narrowing the curriculum lead from 1.9 to 0.75 under the same labelled protocol. Figure 4 changes Infinity-MM S3's 2M result from approximately 59.45 to 59.96. Some Figure 5 baseline levels also change despite unchanged benchmark tables. Unigram statistics and explicit SFT-mixture percentages disappear; existing GPT caption scores are merely rescaled. New GSB rates have conflicting SA1B/DataComp assignments between Figure 8 and the prose.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems, proofs or derivations. The scaling relationships remain empirical; expanded discussion of ranking consistency and human-rating rubrics does not add formal mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The central claims remain high-quality scalable caption construction, logarithmic pretraining scaling, effective SFT curation and curriculum training, and leading 2B/8B benchmark performance. The abstract's explicit use of 'logarithmic' restates a claim already present in v2.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 replaces the explanation linking preference data's General VQA advantage to open-ended examples with an argument that excessive complexity hinders learning and supports curriculum training. v3 also attributes pretrain-advance gains to vision-encoder capacity and captioner quality to distillation. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Azure GPT4o-20240513 and the InternVL2-8B captioner, adds a model card specifying backbone and adapter details, and supplies evaluation prompts and clearer curation groups. Conversely, exact SFT-stage mixture percentages are removed. Software versions, hardware, compute budgets and release-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of ShareGPT4V and ALLaVA as API-based caption-annotation approaches and names Cauldron in data curation. The bibliography and broad research positioning otherwise remain unchanged; ShareGPT4V and Cauldron appear with unresolved citation markers.

P1.justification: v3 expands and rewrites selected data-curation and scaling explanations, reframes Section 5.2, condenses authorship attribution and adds appendix subsections. Most of the introduction, experimental reporting, conclusion and limitations remains intact, preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Several scaling plots receive larger titles, panel labels and revised legends. v3 adds caption-evaluation instructions, a GSB chart, SFT-rating instructions and a model-card table. Table 1 replaces its unigram column with human quality scores, the SFT-composition table is restructured, and appendix showcases and result tables are relocated. These substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens validation through human assessments and makes caption generation and evaluation procedures more explicit. However, it removes exact SFT-mixture proportions and introduces unresolved inconsistencies in central evidence: Figure 5's revised baseline levels disagree with retained tables, while Figure 8 and its prose assign the 87% and 91% GSB rates to different datasets. These tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
